hometown.composition: A small coastal town on Pallet Meadows' upper bench. The main street runs north-south and leaves the town north as the first route toward gym 1; it crosses the east-west street at the Pallet sign's crossroads, the town centre. The Pokemon Center and Poke Mart face each other across the main street just north of the crossroads, where a returning trainer arrives. Five family houses line the cross street's western arm, on the lower ground that looks out over the sea. Oak's Lab stands apart on its own lane on the higher south-east corner. The waystone is beside the crossroads; players spawn on the main street south of the sign.

paving.why: a rock-gym town paved in worked stone: grey andesite streets, rough cobble lanes, a dressed-stone square. Spawn consequences, read from the loaded data: of 4,892 Cobblemon spawn entries only 17 need a base block (quartz in Nether quartz biomes, sand in beach biomes, concrete for Varoom and Revavroom in every overworld biome), and the Cobbleverse datapack repeats Varoom and Revavroom on all 16 concrete colours and adds Terapagos on amethyst in caves. So streets never use concrete. Stone, andesite, cobblestone, mud and prismarine carry no base-block spawn condition: wild Pokemon spawn on them as on any ground in the biome. Hostile mobs need block light 0, so the plan's lamps keep every street block within 14 blocks of a light. Note: the Pokemon Center and Mart donors have white and blue concrete in their roofs and walls, where Varoom can spawn in any town.

plan.reading: The Scar is flat in the way nothing on a mountain is flat: a disc pressed out of Mt Vessu's shoulder, and on it a whole city, dead. Roads of cracked stone brick cross it in a grid, and on every lot between them a house stands in ruin on its foundation: near the old square to the eaves with the roofs gone, further out to the sills, at the rim a course or two. They are the Displaced City's own houses, design for design; a player who has walked the cavern streets knows them. Two towers still stand, one lies full length where it fell, and a stump; broken terrace walls cross the bands between the roads; on the old square the plinth the summit cairn stood on is empty. One avenue runs north across the whole disc and stops at the cliff edge, in the air. Snow and moss, no lamps, no doors, no people. This is where the Displaced City stood; the city is underground now, and this is what it left.

The square is at the head of the hollow with the Centre and the Mart on its north side, backs to the sea wind. From the square the station lane climbs south-west to the one high point on the isle, where the observatory stands clear of the trees with the whole sky over it; the field station is on the lane below it. The east row runs out over the gentler eastern rise, where the spruce houses of the station's people are.

plan.reading: The tunnel brings you out at the north-west corner onto the old summit road, and the road does what it always did: it climbs the ridge to the top of the mountain. It crosses the lower bench, where the lower street runs right round the mountain, then the upper bench and its street, and ends at the foot of the crown, where a stair of nine steps climbs to the summit square on the true top, and the old cairn still marks it and the waystone stands. The two ring streets are the town: houses face out from the benches over the dark, their backs to the mountain, the way houses on a summit do. A lane on the south and one on the east step down from the upper street to the lower. There is no Centre and no Mart. This was a town on a mountain top, and the people in it still live as if it were; nothing here was built to serve travellers. The cherry trees grow on the slopes between the benches and in the dark margins, where they do not compete with the town.
